cards.heading: What discovery protocols do
cards.body: CDP and LLDP let directly connected devices announce themselves: name, model, port, IP address and capabilities. 'show cdp neighbors' maps a network you can't see, such as which switch port leads to which router. They only reach directly connected neighbours; they aren't routed.

cards.heading: CDP
cards.body: Cisco Discovery Protocol is Cisco-proprietary and on by default on Cisco devices. It sends every 60 seconds with a 180-second holdtime.
cards.example:
SW1#show cdp neighbors
Device ID   Local Intrfce   Holdtme   Capability  Platform  Port ID
R1          Gig 0/2         163       R B S I     ISR4321   Gig 0/0/0

cards.heading: LLDP
cards.body: Link Layer Discovery Protocol (IEEE 802.1AB) is the open standard, so non-Cisco devices such as many phones, APs and servers speak it. It's off by default on Cisco devices. It sends every 30 seconds with a 120-second hold time. Transmit and receive can be controlled separately per interface.
cards.example:
lldp run
interface g0/1
 no lldp transmit
 no lldp receive

cards.heading: Detail and verification
cards.body: 'show cdp neighbors detail' adds the neighbour's IP address and software version: handy for finding the address of a device you need to manage. 'show cdp' and 'show lldp' report whether the protocol is running.
cards.example:
SW1#show cdp neighbors detail
Device ID: R1
  IP address: 10.0.0.1
Platform: cisco ISR4321,  Capabilities: Router ...
Interface: GigabitEthernet0/2,  Port ID (outgoing port): GigabitEthernet0/0/0

cards.heading: Security
cards.body: Discovery traffic tells an attacker your models, software versions and addresses. Disable it on ports facing untrusted networks (the internet, guest or public ports): 'no cdp enable' and 'no lldp transmit' per interface, or 'no cdp run' globally.
cards.example:
interface fa0/24
 no cdp enable
 no lldp transmit
